title: Invite people
summary: The Invite people drawer over Members: several emails, one of the four roles, a product or All products, and an optional narrowing to areas, with a sentence that says exactly what the people will and won't see. Sending writes a role binding on each email, asks for a passkey first, emails the invitees and tells every Superadmin.
compare: The drawer opens from the right over Members (dimmed behind); on phone it is a full-screen sheet.

Emails are chips in one focused field: each chip is the raised surface with a line border, so it reads as a removable chip in both themes. The hint says how to separate them. People join when they first sign in with a passkey or SSO at that address (never an email code alone); the drawer head says nothing more than 'Invite people'.

Role is four radio cards in this order: Console access, Product admin, Platform admin, Superadmin. Product editor and Product viewer do not exist. For anyone who isn't a Superadmin, the Platform admin and Superadmin cards are disabled with 'Only a Superadmin can give this role', and All products is disabled too: a Platform admin invites Console access, plus Product admin of the products they admin themselves (Priya: DJDL only, Other states).
Products appears only for Product admin: One product (a product select with its logo) or All products, including ones added later.

Areas appears only for Product admin: 'Every area of <product>' or 'Only these areas' with chips in the area order Core, Licensing, Managed config, Ship builds, Sign-in, Cloud Sync, Commerce, Keys, Settings, Members; only the product's enabled features are offered and a hint names the missing ones (Sign-in and Cloud Sync aren't on for Diceroll).
The preview sentence updates with every choice and names the addresses by their local part (hana@ and theo@ will manage Ship builds and Commerce in Diceroll).

The primary button asks for the passkey (fingerprint glyph, 'Passkey required' as its title) and counts only valid addresses: 'Invite 2 people'. An invalid address is an error chip with a message under the field that names the address and the fix and says it isn't counted. Two fact lines above the footer say what sending does: 'Expires Oct 14' and 'Every Superadmin is told'. Cancel is the outline button in both themes; idle selects and unselected radios are raised, not tinted.
After sending with email on, the drawer closes, a toast says 'Invited 2 people' with Undo (which removes both invites); each address is a row in Members (Other states).

An address that is already a member becomes a member chip (initials) with a note naming the person, their current roles and what is added; no invite is sent and the button says so: 'Invite 1 person and update 1'. An address an SSO rule already covers works the same way, and a repeated address merges into one chip.

When email delivery is off, the button reads 'Create invite links' and the result lists each address with its read-only link and a Copy button, says nothing was emailed, and gives the expiry (Oct 14, 7 days); Done closes it (Other states).
Nobody can grant more than they hold: a Product admin of Diceroll inviting from Product → Settings → Members sees only Diceroll and only the areas they have.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink; focus, hover, checked and selected take the accent of the service the element references (B17), never a status colour; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Dialog and drawer head (B4): a 3px rule in the origin's accent along the top (none on a destructive or cautious confirmation), a head band with a hairline, one leading glyph or none (severity on a confirmation, the subject's mark on a record, never a service tile), title at or under 20/28; blurred backdrop with a flat fallback under reduced transparency.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fix applied: chips read as chips in light, and the error, already-a-member, invite-link, after-send and Platform admin states are drawn.

findings.issue: In light theme the email chips have no fill or border inside the focused lavender field, so the addresses read as plain text.
findings.resolution: Chips are now the raised surface with a strong line border (white in light, raised in dark) inside the sunken, focused field. Checked in both themes.

findings.issue: No error state: an invalid address, a duplicate, an existing member or an address an SSO rule covers, and how the button count reacts.
findings.resolution: The main drawer has a third chip, 'marta@example', in error form (danger outline and tint, alert icon) and an error under the field naming the address and the fix; it isn't counted, so the button still reads 'Invite 2 people'. Other states draws an existing member (Felix, a member chip and a note saying what is added, button 'Invite 1 person and update 1'); the caption covers rule-covered and repeated addresses. Felix stands in for the reviewer's Lucía example because Lucía already holds Ship builds and Commerce in Diceroll, so inviting her would add nothing. The preview also stops guessing names: 'hana@example.com and theo@example.com will manage…'.

findings.issue: Email delivery off ('Create invite links' with one copyable link per address) and the result after sending aren't drawn.
findings.resolution: Other states: the footer with 'Create invite links', then 'Invite links for 2 people' with each address, its role, a read-only link and Copy, the Oct 14 expiry (7 days, per the plan) and Done. After sending with email on: the 'Invited 2 people' toast with Undo and the two rows waiting for first sign-in.

findings.issue: The compare implies a Platform admin can give Product admin of any product; the non-Superadmin view isn't drawn.
findings.resolution: Compare corrected: a Platform admin invites Console access, plus Product admin of products they admin. Priya's view is drawn: Console access on, Product admin limited to DJDL, Platform admin and Superadmin disabled with 'Only a Superadmin can give this role', All products disabled with the reason.

findings.issue: Cancel is a filled grey button in light and borderless in dark; unselected radios and the product select look disabled in light.
findings.resolution: Cancel is the outline button in both themes (also in the SSO rule editor). In the drawer, idle selects and unselected radio boxes use the raised surface with their line border.

findings.issue: The drawer title ranked no higher than the section labels, and the two footer notes said the same thing.
findings.resolution: Title is 20/28 (the console draws Rubik at 700 only, so not 600) with the 24px body padding under the head; field labels are one muted 12px bold style; the notes merge into one line above the footer ('Emails each invite and tells every Superadmin. Expires Oct 14.'); 'Passkey required' stays on the primary button only (fingerprint glyph, title and aria-label).

findings.issue: The preview and toast restated the chips and the list; four stacked role cards pushed Products and Areas below the fold on phone.
findings.resolution: Preview reads 'hana@ and theo@ will manage Ship builds and Commerce in Diceroll' (exclusions sentence dropped); the toast is 'Invited 2 people' with Undo; on phone Role is a 2x2 grid of tiles with the picked role's words once below (.choices.tiles-phone); the drawer foot is sticky on phone (.sticky-foot, rested at the sheet's end in shots); 32px sits under the drawer frame before Other states.

findings.issue: The Members page behind the drawer repeated the Members screen's spacing and duplication defects.
findings.resolution: The page behind takes the same fixes as Members (56px rows, trimmed banner, no footer, 24px gaps, solid chips, folded last sign-in).

findings.issue: Tables stretched to about 1615px at 1920, so cells sat 275px or more apart and the page widths differed across the area.
findings.resolution: Pages cap at one content width, centred: 1280px for tables, 1136px for forms and status pages (kit .page.cap-table, .page.cap-form).

findings.issue: Small muted mono keys, dates and helper text carried facts at subtle colour and under 12px; disabled buttons were near invisible; row-menu targets were 28px.
findings.resolution: Fact-bearing small text moves to the muted token and 12px or more; the light subtle token is #4f586d (4.5:1 or better on every surface in both themes); disabled buttons keep a visible border at 0.6 opacity (0.8 on primary); the row-menu trigger is 32px with a 44px hit area (44px on phone); colour-only Adds and Joins carry a glyph.

findings.issue: Other states left 120 to 700px of dead space beside shorter cards, and the captions narrated layout.
findings.resolution: Other states sit on one equal-width grid (3 columns from desktop, 2 on tablet, 1 on phone) with the page's card primitive; captions name the state and its trigger.

findings.issue: Add new states for send failure, duplicate pending invite and too many addresses, and rename the button 'Invite 1 and update 1 member'.
findings.resolution: declined: The content, states and structure are to be kept in this pass, and the button label is existing copy.

findings.issue: h1 plus tabs is the kit's pattern; role names and the glossary are owner and consolidation-plan decisions.
findings.resolution: declined: Change the h1 to match each tab, add breadcrumbs on platform pages, or add 'Rename Console access to Viewer' and a glossary entry.

findings.issue: Date and glossary rules belong to the copy rules and the consolidation plan, not to a spacing pass.
findings.resolution: declined: Rewrite dates to 'relative within 7 days, else Oct 6, year only when not current' and add the 'Product admin = one product or all' glossary note.
